messages:
jess: noticing a weird provisioning tail this morning in eu-west1 — a bunch of GPU pods stuck in Pending for ~30s then succeed. Seen across 3 AZs.

carlos: saw that too. node allocs show high io_wait around 03:10 UTC. NVMe iops spike but no user traffic change.

mei: checking node telemetry now — scrubber tasks kicked exactly at 03:09 on a large fraction of nodes. scrub concurrency spiked to 12.

sahil: hmm we stagger scrubs by region? thought EU window was randomized. any recent cron change?

jess: nope no deploys to janitor in last 48h. but an overlay rollout yesterday bumped default concurrency in the cleaner config (value: 12 -> 16). maybe a flag flip.

ops-bot: deploy: janitor-service v2.8.1 rolled to eu-west1 at 2026-03-18T22:40:12Z by nora — jobs: cleaner-concurrency default=16

nora: that was to speed up backlog clearing after the big reclaim. didn't think about iops impact on GPU attach. my bad. :grimacing:

carlos: can we confirm correlation? iops graph attached to nodes shows scrub bursts align with GPU attach queues — queue depth jumps, kubelet CPU goes up, attach waits.

mei: I pulled logs from 10 affected nodes. excerpt: 
```
Mar 19 03:09:12 scrubber[4213]: start shard-clean id=sh-7 concurrency=16
Mar 19 03:09:17 kernel: nvme0n1: io_queue_depth 1024 -> 4096
Mar 19 03:09:22 kubelet: attach-detach-controller: attach wait 32000ms for pod/p-123
```

jess: exact. also see a handful of transient readonly remounts on nvme (<1% of nodes) during peak iops — likely firmware hitting internal throttles, causing latency tail.

sahil: two-prong mitigation: 1) immediately reduce cleaner concurrency in eu-west1 to 4, 2) add a soft QoS throttle on janitor to cap iops contribution.

nora: I'll roll a hotfix flag. propose config patch: `cleaner.concurrency: 4` for eu-west1 only. Want me to push?

carlos: yes. also add a temp admission controller tweak to prefer nodes with scrub_occupancy < 0.2 for gpu pods. simple predicate. buys us time.

mei: I can add the predicate as a small mutating webhook change — low risk. will prepare PR.

jess: and schedule to revert after we examine firmware counters with vendor. we should also add a metric: scrub_iops_per_node and alert when > 20k sustained for 30s.

nora: pushing flag now to eu-west1 canaries (20% of nodes). will monitor for next 20m. :rocket:

ops-bot: canary rollout starting: janitor-service flag patch to eu-west1-canary at 2026-03-19T03:20:05Z

carlos: early telemetry: canary nodes iops down ~60%, gpu attach Pending latencies back to baseline for those nodes. good signal.

mei: PR for admission predicate: https://git.redwood.dev/infra/gatekeeper/pull/412 — adds node label check `scrub_occupancy` <0.2 and ties to GPU workload class.

jess: nice. nora leave the global default at 16 for other regions for now? APAC had large backlog, but we can target patch per-region.

nora: correct — only eu-west1 reduced so far. I'll open a follow-up runbook entry: "hotfix: reduce janitor concurrency if iops tail causes GPU attach > 200ms".

sahil: long term we should: 1) make cleaner iops-aware (throttle when nvme_latency_p95 > X), 2) split scrub windows away from critical batch attach window (avoid 03:00-04:00), 3) vendor firmware check for internal thermal/queue throttling.

carlos: also consider opportunistic prefetch: if node has upcoming GPU attach, pause heavy janitor ops on that node for 60s. small coordination layer.

jess: agreed. action items: nora (hotfix region flag push + runbook) ; mei (admission predicate PR + roll); carlos (dashboard + alert for scrub_iops_per_node); sahil (design doc for iops-aware cleaner) ; i'll loop vendor for firmware telemetry.

nora: done — flag rolled to canary, monitoring. I'll post an update in 15m.

ops-bot: metric alert suppressed: scrub_iops > 20000 (eu-west1) for nodepool-west-a — suppression due to hotfix rollout until 03:50 UTC

mei: PR merged and gatekeeper rolled to canary. observing pod scheduling shift away from scrub-heavy nodes on canary cluster.

carlos: good. capturing this as postmortem note: short term change caused unintended global pressure — need per-region defaults and a preflight for iops-sensitive services before changing cleaner defaults.

jess: thanks all. if we get another spike after full rollout we revert and throttle further.

nora: update 03:45 UTC: no further attach delays seen in canary, rolling eu-west1 full patch in 5m.

sahil: will start doc skeleton for iops-aware cleaner design.

jess: I'll create a brief ops ticket for vendor firmware checks.

nora: closing loop — runbook draft: https://docs.redwood.dev/runbooks/janitor-io-spike — please review and add any missing checks.

carlos: quick note for billing: lowering concurrency will delay reclaim and could increase ephemeral storage costs by ~0.6% this week. flag for finance?

jess: yep notify finance channel after full rollout.

nora: full eu-west1 rollout completed at 03:52 UTC. monitoring continues. :white_check_mark:
